messages:
maya: Kicking off a short thread on an alternate approach to BYOK+SOC2 evidence: what if we offer an immutable append-only audit ledger (Merkle-chained daily roots) + tiered retention lanes (hot/warm/cold) and separate access policies per lane? Thoughts?

sam: Security thumbs-up for immutable roots and signed attestations. Key questions: who signs roots (Redwood HSM vs customer HSM) and how do we prove non-repudiation after customer rotates keys?

zhen: Eng: doable. Runtime can emit daily manifests (hashes only) and chain them. Payloads stored in lanes; hot lane = decryptable on-demand, cold lane = encrypted w/KEK + require escrow retrieval. Storage lifecycle policies manage lane transitions.

gita: Product: this gives us flexibility to sell "retention lanes" as SKUs: Standard (90d sampled hot + 1y warm hashed), Compliance (1y hot with escrow), Forensics (7y cold with escrow+notary). Buyers like predictable tiers.

eli: Ops: operations impact: retrieval SLAs vary by lane. Hot <4h, Warm <24h, Cold+escrow up to 7d. Need automated playbooks for lane promotions and for legal-hold overrides. Also need cost attribution per project.

nina: CS: customers ask for auditor-friendly artifacts. Manifests + merkle proofs are good, but auditors often want readable logs. Suggest we include a "readable index" (metadata rows) that stays in hot/warm for shorter windows.

sam: Security caveat: if customer insists on customer-HSM signing of daily roots, we must support a signing endpoint and require an OIDC token from the operator. That avoids Redwood signing if customer mandates.

zhen: Implementation sketch: - add retention_lanes: [hot,warm,cold] - daily_root: {root_hash, signer, sig_ts} - payload pointer index links to lane+blob_id - provide /evidence/bundle?start=..&end=.. returns manifest+merkle proofs+retrieve token

gita: Pricing idea: base API + hot-retention price per GB-month + warm/cold retrieval surcharge + escrow handling fee. Also add a compliance SLA premium for attestation + notary.

eli: Runbook notes: - legal-hold API toggles lane transitions - rotation handling: pre-rotation export webhook -> if customer declines, mark applicable blobs as unrecoverable and generate signed attestation.

nina: Pilot plan: offer to FinCorp and Healthly as a "retention lanes beta". FinCorp wants customer-HSM signing; Healthly prefers Redwood-managed signing. Good test of both flows.

sam: Open risks: cross-region custody (EU data residency), escrow trust models, and auditor acceptance of hashed-only archives. We should validate with 2 external auditors before GA.

zhen: Est. work: daily manifests + lanes lifecycle + basic retrieval = 2 sprints. Customer-HSM signing + escrow connector + pricing = 3 sprints.

maya: Candidate launch checklist: API for lane config, daily merkle roots, evidence bundle API, lane SLA table, pricing SKUs, legal escrow template, pilot signups. I'll draft RFC and assign owners. Anyone object?

ops-bot: Created infra ticket INF-5099 for retention lanes storage lifecycle and HSM endpoint (https://redwood.internal/INF-5099) :robot_face:

maya: No objections heard. Proceeding to RFC. Will schedule auditor sessions and legal review. Thanks all.
